claims.text: Adding 0.5 wt% Y to CoCrFeNiAl-based HEA bond coats will promote formation of Y2O3 dispersoids.
The Y2O3 dispersoids will preferentially occur at grain boundaries and the bond-coat/oxide interface.
Y addition will enhance the adhesion of the protective thermally grown oxide scale.
Y addition will improve the uniformity of the protective thermally grown oxide scale.
The reactive-element effect of Y will reduce oxygen diffusion through the oxide scale.
Y will stabilize the bond-coat/oxide interface.
Reduced oxygen diffusion and interface stabilization will produce a slower-growing oxide scale.
The Y-modified bond coat will have slower oxidation kinetics than an otherwise comparable Y-free bond coat.
The Y-modified bond coat will form a thinner oxide scale than an otherwise comparable Y-free bond coat.
The Y-modified bond coat will exhibit less oxide-scale spallation than an otherwise comparable Y-free bond coat.
Reduced oxide growth and spallation will improve coating durability and reliability.
The beneficial effect of 0.5 wt% Y is expected to persist near 1100 °C in oxidizing atmospheres during prolonged exposure and typical thermal cycling.
Extreme thermal cycling or operation outside the stated processing or service envelope may reduce the effectiveness of Y addition.
An as-cast CoCrFeNiAl-based HEA bond coat typically has a coarse-grained microstructure.
